rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are idol worshippers, and the clear proof is Muhammad, whose coming ended their prior persistence in disbelief, though some believed and others remained disbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمراد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لم يتركوا كفرهم حتى يبعث محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munfakkīn means separated from disbelief; the omitted object is understood from the relative phrase alladhīna kafarū.
rows.anchor: منفصلين عن الكفر وحذف لأن صلة الذين تدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-rajul means those closest to him, while Ahl al-Islam denotes those who profess Islam.
rows.anchor: وأهل الرجل أخص الناس به وأهل الإسلام من يدين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is Muhammad and stands in apposition to the clear proof; he recites papers or scrolls purified of falsehood.
rows.anchor: أى محمد عليه السلام وهو بدل من البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written contents are in the scrolls and are upright, speaking with truth and justice.
rows.anchor: مكتوبات ﴿ قيمة ﴾ مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the proof arrived, some scripturalists denied Muhammad out of envy and hostility and some believed; they are singled out because scripture had made them aware of him, so their division makes those without scripture still more implicated.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من أنكر نبوته بغيا وحدا ومنهم من آمن وإثما أفرد أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands were already in the Torah and Gospel: worship God alone without association or hypocrisy, turn from false religions as believers in all messengers, establish prayer, and give alms; this is the upright religious community.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما أمروا ﴾ يعنى فى التوراة والانجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥunafāʾ means believing in all the messengers while inclining away from false religions.
rows.anchor: مؤمنين بجميع الرسل مائلين عن الأديان الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ hamz-reads the two forms, while al-Farrāʾ favors lightening; nabī and bariyya are established conventional lightened forms that displaced their original forms.
rows.anchor: ونافع بهمزهما والفراء على التخفيف والنبى والبرية مما استمر الاستعمال على تخفيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is lasting residence in gardens with rivers, where they remain forever; God is pleased by accepting their deeds and they are pleased with the reward.
rows.anchor: بقبول أعمالهم ﴿ ورضوا عنه ﴾ بثوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That pleasure belongs to whoever fears the Lord; barriyya may derive from God creating, or from soil, though al-Zajjāj rejects the soil derivation because the word is not read with hamza.
rows.anchor: لمن خشي ربه ﴾ وقوله خير البرية يدل على فضل المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression the best of creation indicates that believing humans have precedence over angels; barriyya means creation and is derived from God bringing creation into being.
rows.anchor: خير البرية يدل على فضل المؤمنين من البشر على الملائكة لأن البرية الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is shaken with its ultimate, severe shaking, after which there is no further quake.
rows.anchor: حركت زلزالها الشديد الذى ليس بعده زلزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the first zāy treats zalzāl as a noun, whereas the kasra reading is the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرئ بفتح الزاى فالمكسور مصدر والمفتوح اسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth brings out its treasures and its dead; athqāl are household goods, and buried things inside the earth are figuratively its burdens.
rows.anchor: أى كنوزها وموتاها جمع ثقل وهو متاع البيت جعل ما فى جوفها من الدفائن أثقالا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person asks what is wrong with the earth because it has violently shaken and expelled what was inside; this occurs at the second trumpet when the dead emerge alive, stunning people with the terrible event.
rows.anchor: وذلك عند النفخة الثانية حين تزلزل وتلفظ موتاها أحياء فيقولون ذلك لما يهرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view assigns the question to disbelievers, who had denied resurrection; believers instead say this is what the Merciful promised and the messengers spoke truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذا قول الكافر لأنه كان لا يؤمن بالبعث فأما المؤمن فيقول هذا ما وعد الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question resembles the people asking who raised them from their resting place.
rows.anchor: كما يقولون من بعثنا من مرقدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm idhin is an apposition to idhā and governs the clause; the earth tells people its news, with the audience omitted because the focus is on reporting the news.
rows.anchor: بدل من إذا وناصبها ﴿ تحدث ﴾ أى تحدث الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says God gives the earth speech so it reports the good and evil people did upon it.
rows.anchor: قيل ينطقها الله وتخبر بما عمل عليها من خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the earth will testify for each person to what that person did on its surface.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث تشهد على كل واحد بما علم على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth reports because the Lord inspired or instructed it to do so.
rows.anchor: أى تحدث أخبارها بسبب ايحاء ربك لها أى إليها وأمره اياها بالتحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People leave their graves for the gathering place in scattered groups; this may mean secure white-faced people and terrified black-faced people, or groups taking separate routes toward Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: أشتاتا يتفرق بهم طريقا الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing their deeds means seeing the recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ليروا أعمالهم ﴾ أى جزاء أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dharra is a tiny ant; khayran is an accusative specification, and seeing the deed means seeing its reward.
rows.anchor: نملة ضغيرة ﴿ خيرا ﴾ تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view applies this verse to disbelievers and the preceding verse to believers.
rows.anchor: قيل هذا فى الكفار والأول فى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted anecdote says an Arab placed khayran after yarahu; when questioned, he replied that he had advanced and delayed.
rows.anchor: أن اعرابيا أخر خيرا يره فقيل له فدمت وأخرت فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's grandfather of al-Farazdaq came asking for recitation; after hearing the verse he said it was enough, and it was called the wisest verse and al-Jāmiʿa.
rows.anchor: أن جد الفرزدق أتاه عليه السلام ليستقرئه فقرأ عليه هذه الآية فقال حسبى حسبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses reach a group of enemies; the pronoun may refer to the time, the raid location, or the horses understood from al-ʿādiyāt, and wast means to penetrate the middle.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فوسطن به ﴾ بذلك الوقت ﴿ جمعا ﴾ من جموع الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atharna is coordinated with the implied verb sequence represented by the active participle: the horses ran, sparked, raided, and raised dust, completing the oath sequence.
rows.anchor: وعطف فأثرن على الفعل الذى وضع اسم الفاعل موضعه لأن المعنى واللاتى عدون فأورين فأغرن فأثرن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the human as witness to his own ingratitude; another takes God as witnessing the human's ingratitude as a threat.
rows.anchor: على كنوده ﴿ لشهيد ﴾ يشهد على نفسه أو وأن الله على كنوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the human is miserly because of his love of wealth; another says he is intensely attached to wealth but weak in worship of God.
rows.anchor: لأجل حب المال لبخيل ممسك أو أنه لحب المال لقوى وهو لحب عبادة الله ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question addresses the human: when what is in the graves is brought up, the dead are resurrected.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفلا يعلم ﴾ الإنسان ﴿ إذا بعثر ﴾ بعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in the breasts is sifted so that its good and evil are distinguished.
rows.anchor: ميز ما فيها من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows them and will repay their good and evil deeds; He is specified as knowing them that day because recompense takes place then, though He knows them at all times.
rows.anchor: لعالم فيجازيهم على أعمالهم من الخير والشر وخص يومئذ بالذكر وهو عالم بهم فى جميع الأزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qāriʿa is the subject of a nominal sentence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ القارعة ﴾ مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second mā is a subject and al-qāriʿa its predicate; the clause predicates the first subject, and repetition magnifies the event instead of saying simply what it is.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما ﴾ مبتدأ ثان ﴿ القارعة ﴾ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks what thing could inform you of the event and from where you would know it.
rows.anchor: أى أى شئ أعلمك ما هى ومن أين علمت ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is accusative under an implied verb indicated by al-qāriʿa, as if it strikes on that day; people resemble moths in number, scattering, weakness, abasement, and flight toward the caller from every side like moths toward fire.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث ﴾ شبههم بالفراش في الكثرة والانتشار والضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called farāsh because they spread and scatter.
rows.anchor: وسمى فراشا لتفرشه وانتشاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains resemble dyed wool because they have different colors, including white and red streaks; fluffed wool conveys their fragments dispersing.
rows.anchor: وهو الصوف المصبغ ألوانا لأنها ألوان ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Abyss, and the final hāʾ is the pause marker; the next verse explains it.
rows.anchor: الضمير يعود إلى هاوية والهاء للسكت ثم فسرها فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire has reached the utmost limit of heat.
rows.anchor: بلغت النهاية فى الحرارة والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes and alerts the person who should not make accumulating worldly things the whole of his concern while neglecting religion; the bad outcome will be known at death.
rows.anchor: ردع وتنبيه على أنه لا ينبغى للناظر لنفسه أن تكون الدنيا تجميع همه ولا يهتم بدينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about what they pursued will be known at the moment of death.
rows.anchor: ﴿ سوف تعلمون ﴾ عند النزع سوء عاقبة ما كنتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second warning says they will know the outcome in their graves.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم كلا سوف تعلمون ﴾ فى القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating kallā intensifies the rebuke as warning and intimidation; the omitted apodosis means that certainty about what lies ahead would have prevented rivalry or prompted indescribable action.
rows.anchor: تكرير الردع للانذار والتخريف ﴿ لو تعلمون ﴾ جواب لو محذوف أى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm al-yaqīn is knowledge of the certain matter; their rivalry shows they are astray and ignorant.
rows.anchor: علم الأمر اليقين أى كعلمكم ما تستيقنونه من الأمور لما ألهاكم التكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is the answer to an omitted oath, whose purpose is to strengthen the threat.
rows.anchor: هو جواب قسم محذوف والقسم لتوكيد الوعيد

rows.speaker: الشامي، علي
rows.claim: The Shamī and ʿAlī reading has ḍamma on tāʾ, making the people be shown the Hellfire.
rows.anchor: لترون بضم التاء شامى وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the warning with thumma intensifies the threat and terror; alternatively, the first sight is by the heart and the second by the eyes.
rows.anchor: كرره معطوفا بثم تغليظا فى التهديد وزيادة فى التهويل أو الأول بالقلب والثانى بالعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAyn al-yaqīn is direct vision, the very essence and purest form of certainty.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عين اليقين ﴾ أى الرؤية التى هى نفس اليقين وخالصته

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains the blessing as security and health, asking how they were spent.
rows.anchor: عن الأمن والصحة فيم أفنيتموهما عن ابن مسعود رضى الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is the pleasurable luxuries that distracted people from religion and its duties.
rows.anchor: وقيل عن التنعيم الذى شغلكم الالتذاذ به عن الدين وتكاليفه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the blessing is a shelter, clothing, and a morsel of food; the account is also transmitted as a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ما سوى كن يؤويه وثوب يواريه وكسرة تقويه وقد روى مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is the sentence's subject and the phrase about every slanderer gives its predicate; hamz means backbiting and lamz means fault-finding face to face, habits indicated by the verb forms.
rows.anchor: أى الذى يعيب الناس من خلفهم ﴿ لمزة ﴾ أى من يعيهم مواجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about al-Akhnaṣ ibn Sharīq, whose habit was backbiting and disparagement, or about Umayya ibn Khalaf or al-Walīd; the occasion may be specific while the warning applies to everyone who does this.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت فى الأخنس بن شريق وكانت عادته الغيبة والوقيعة وقيل فى أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the hoarder's presumption: the one who amassed wealth will certainly be cast into the crushing fire, whose nature is to crush whatever is thrown into it.
rows.anchor: ردع له عن حسبانه ﴿ لينبذن ﴾ أى الذى جمع ﴿ في الحطمة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question what the Hutama is expresses amazement and magnifies its severity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وما أدراك ما الحطمة ﴾ تعجيب وتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nār Allāh is the predicate of an omitted subject, with al-mūqada describing the fire.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أى هى نار الله ﴿ الموقدة ﴾ نعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire penetrates the body until it reaches the heart's center, the most delicate and pain-sensitive part, so its arrival there is especially agonizing.
rows.anchor: تدخل فى أجوافهم حتى تصل إلى صدورهم وتطلع على أفئدتهم وهى أوساط القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation singles out the hearts because they are the sites of disbelief and corrupt beliefs; the fire's looking upon them means enclosing them.
rows.anchor: وقيل خص الأفئدة لأنها مواطن الكفر والعقائد الفاسدة ومعنى اطلاع النار عليها أنها تشتمل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the fire or the Hutama, and muʾṣada means shut and closed over them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنها عليهم ﴾ أى النار أ والحطمة ﴿ مؤصدة ﴾ مطبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kūfan readers other than Ḥafṣ read ʿumud with two ḍammas; the others read ʿamad, two plural forms of ʿimād, like ihāb/uhub and ḥimār/ḥumur.
rows.anchor: بضمتين كوفى غير حفص الباقون فى عمد وهما لغتان فى جمع عماد كاهاب وأهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doors are shut and long pillars are extended across them to secure them further.
rows.anchor: توصد عليهم الأبواب وتمدد على الأبواب العمد استيثاقا فى استيثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith contrasts the alert, deliberate, learned, scrupulous believer with the slanderous, careless hypocrite who gathers and spends without concern.
rows.anchor: فى الحديث المؤمن كيس فطن وقاف متثبت لا يعجل عالم ورع والمنافق همزة لمزة حطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa is accusative with faʿala, not araʾayta, since it carries interrogative force; the clause supplies araʾayta's two objects, and the question expresses wonder at God's sign witnessed by the Arabs.
rows.anchor: كيف فى موضع نصب بفعل لا بألم تر لما فى كيف من معنى الاستفهام والجملة سدت مسد مفعولى تر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee saw the effects of God's action against the Abyssinians and heard mass-transmitted reports, which stand in for eyewitnessing.
rows.anchor: إنك رأيت آثار صنع الله بالحبشة وسمعت الأخبار به متواترا فقامت لك مقام المشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha, governor of Yemen under the Najāshī Aṣḥama, built al-Qullays in Ṣanʿāʾ to divert pilgrims; a man from Kināna defiled it at night, and another report says Arabs lit a fire whose windblown sparks burned it.
rows.anchor: أن أبرهة بن الصباح ملك اليمن من قبل اصحمة النجاشى بنى كنيسة بصنعاء وسماها القليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angered by the incident, Abraha swore to demolish the Kaaba and marched with the Abyssinians and elephants, including the strong elephant Maḥmūd and twelve others.
rows.anchor: فحلف ليهدمن الكعبة فخرج بالحبشة ومعه قيل اسمه محمود وكان قويا عظيما واثنا عشر فيلا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When directed toward the sanctuary the elephant knelt and would not move, but it ran when turned toward Yemen; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib offered Abraha a third of Tihāma's wealth to withdraw, but he refused.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغ المغمس خرج إليه عبد المطلب وعرض عليه ثلث أموال تهامة ليرجع فأبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent birds carrying three stones each, one in its beak and two on its feet; lentil-to-chickpea-sized stones bore victims' names and pierced each man through, making the army flee and die.
rows.anchor: فأرسل الله طيرا مع كل طائر حجر فى منقاره وحجران فى رجليه أكبر من العدسة وأصغر من الحمصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha's chest split around his heart before he died; his minister Abū Yaksūm escaped, but a bird followed and dropped a stone that killed him before the Najāshī.
rows.anchor: وما مات أبرهة حتى انصدع صدره عن قلبه وانفلت وزيره أبو يكسوم وطائر يحلق فوقه حتى بلغ النجاشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Abraha seized two hundred of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's camels; the dignified, handsome Quraysh leader asked for them, prompting Abraha to rebuke him for caring for camels rather than the sacred House.
rows.anchor: وروى أن أبرهة أخذ لعبد المطلب مائتى بعير فخرج إليه فيها فعظم فى عينه وكان رجلا جسيما وسيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib answered that he owned the camels while the House had a Lord who would protect it; he was described as feeding people in the lowlands and wild animals in the mountains.
rows.anchor: أنا رب الإبل وللبيت رب سيمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadlīl means making a plan wasted and void; Imruʾ al-Qays was called al-Malik al-Ḍalīl because his father's kingdom was lost.
rows.anchor: فى تضييع وإبطال يقال ضلل كيده إذا جعله ضالا ضائعا وقيل لامرئ القيس الملك الضليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first plot was building al-Qullays to redirect pilgrims, defeated when it burned; the second was attacking the House, defeated by the birds.
rows.anchor: يعنى أنهم كادوا البيت أو ببناء القليس ليصرفوا وجو الحاج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abābīl means groups, with ibāla as its singular; al-Zajjāj explains them as groups arriving from here and there.
rows.anchor: خزائق الواحدة ابالة قال الزجاج جماعات من ههنا وجماعات من ههنا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa reads yarmeehim, with a masculine verb referring either to God or to the birds, since a collective noun may be masculine though it can agree by meaning in the feminine.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة رضى الله عنه يرميهم أى الله أو الطير لأنه اسم جمع مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl is a loanword from Persian sang-gil; according to the majority it means baked brick.
rows.anchor: هو معرب من سنككل وعليه الجمهور أي الآجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were made like crop straw eaten by worms.
rows.anchor: زرع أكله الدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-īlāf attaches to falyaʿbudū; the fāʾ reflects a conditional sense: if they will not worship for all God's countless favors, let them worship for this manifest one.
rows.anchor: لأجل إيلافهم الرحلتين ودخلت الفاء لما فى الكلام من معنى الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it attaches to the preceding verse: God destroyed the Abyssinians for Quraysh's security and affinity, so people would respect them and protect their two journeys.
rows.anchor: أو بما قبله أى فجعلهم كعصف مأكول لا يلاف قريش يعنى ان ذلك الاتلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This attachment is like poetic tadmin, where a line's meaning depends on the preceding line; Ubayy's codex joined the sūras without a divider, and al-Kisāʾī is reported to omit the basmala between them.
rows.anchor: وهما فى مصحف أبى سورة واحدة بلا فصل ويروى عن الكسائى ترك التسمية بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading is explained as an imperative to marvel at Quraysh's security; the Shāmī reading has īlāf as those who make Quraysh familiar.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى أعجبوا لا يلاف قريش لالاف قريش شامى أى المؤلفة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word īlāf is linked to the root alafa, with forms alfan and īlāfan.
rows.anchor: وقيل يقال ألفته ألفا والافا وقريش ولد النضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are Nadr ibn Kināna's descendants; the name may derive from a large sea creature that attacks ships and is released only by fire, with the diminutive conveying greatness and strength.
rows.anchor: وقريش ولد النضر بن كنانة سموه بتصغير القرش وهو دابة عظيمة فى البحر تعبث بالسفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects Quraysh with gathering and earning, since they earned through trade and traveled abroad.
rows.anchor: وقيل من القرش وهو الجمع والكسب لأنهم كانوا كسابين بتجاراتهم وضربهم فى البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted īlāf is followed by its specification as the two journeys to magnify the bond and remind Quraysh of the blessing; journey is the object of īlāfihim, singular in wording to avoid ambiguity.
rows.anchor: أطلق الإيلاف ثم أبدل عنه المقيد بالرحلتين تفخيما لأمر الإيلاف وتذكيرا لعظيم النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh traveled in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria for provisions and trade; their journeys were secure because they belonged to God's sanctuary, unlike other travelers who faced raids.
rows.anchor: وكانت لقريش رحلتان يرحلون فى الشتاء إلى اليمن وفى الصيف إلى الشام فيتمارون ويتجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite forms hunger and fear convey their severity; the journeys relieved severe hunger that preceded them and secured them from great danger.
rows.anchor: والتنكير فى جوع وخوف لشدتهما يعنى أطعمهم بالرحلتين من جوع شديد كانوا فيه قبلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The danger may be the People of the Elephant or fear of being seized in their town and on their travels.
rows.anchor: وآمنهم من خوف عظيم وهو خوف أصحاب الفيل أو خوف التخطف فى بلدهم ومسايرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a crisis made them eat carrion and burned bones; God protected them from leprosy in their town, and another view attributes all of this to Abraham's supplication.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا قد أصابتهم شدة حتى أكلوا الجيف والعظام المحرقة آمنهم من خوف الجذام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings of food and security are also said to have come through Abraham's prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل ذلك كله بدعاء إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the listener recognizes who denies recompense, if he does not already know.
rows.anchor: أى هل عرفت الذى يكذب بالجزاء من هو ان لم تعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier of recompense drives the orphan away harshly, treating him with roughness and insult.
rows.anchor: أ ى يدفعه دفعا عنيفا بجفوه وأذى ويرده ردا قبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He neither urges his household to feed the poor nor offers help himself; harming the vulnerable and withholding kindness show disbelief in recompense, since belief would make him fear God's punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعث أهله على بذل طعام المسكين جعل علم التكذيب بالجزاء منع المعروف والاقدام على إيذاء الضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawthar is an intensive form meaning overwhelming abundance; one reported identification is a river in Paradise, with banks of emerald and silver vessels.
rows.anchor: هو فوعل من الكثرة وهو المفرط الكثرة وقيل هو نهر في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly river is described as sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, colder than snow, and softer than butter.
rows.anchor: أحلى من العسل وأشد بياضا من اللبن وأبرد من الثلج وألين من الزبد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says kawthar means abundant good; when told others identify it as a river in Paradise, he replied that the river is part of abundant good.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما هو الخير الكثير فقيل له ان ناسا يقولون هو نهر فى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer means worshipping the Lord who honored and protected the Prophet, rather than relying on people's favors; sacrifice to God in His name opposes those who sacrifice to idols.
rows.anchor: فاعبد ربك الذي أعزك باعطائه وشرفك وصانك من منن الخلق مراغما لقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's hater is the one among his people who resents his opposition; that person is cut off from every good, while the Prophet's believing descendants and enduring remembrance make him far from abtar.
rows.anchor: ان من أبغضك من قومك بمخالفتك لهم ﴿ هو الأبتر ﴾ المنقطع عن كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who called the Prophet abtar; the word also means one without offspring.
rows.anchor: قيل نزلت في العاص بن وائل سماه الأبتر والابتر الذي لا عقب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing syntax is parsed as two predicates, with huwa as a separating pronoun.
rows.anchor: وهو خبران وهو فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to particular Quraysh disbelievers whom God knew would not believe.
rows.anchor: المخاطبون كفرة مخصوصون قد علم الله أنهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of Quraysh proposed that Muhammad follow their religion and they follow his for alternating years; he rejected associating partners with God, and they then asked him to touch an idol so they could believe him.
rows.anchor: روى أن رهطا من قريش قالوا يا محمد هلم فاتبع ديننا ونتبع دينك تعبد آلهتنا سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the revelation, Muhammad went to the Sacred Mosque, recited the sūra before Quraysh's leaders, and they despaired.
rows.anchor: فغدا إلى المسجد الحرام وفيه الملأ من قريش فقرأ عليم فآيسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not a worshipper of what the addressees worship in his present state.
rows.anchor: أى لست في حالي هذه عابد ما تعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are not worshipping God at the present time.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا أنتم عابدون ﴾ الساعة ﴿ ما أعبد ﴾ يعني الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet will not worship what they worship in any future time.
rows.anchor: ولا أعبد فيما استقبل من الزمان ما عبدتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not worship what the Prophet worships in the future; mā may emphasize the quality, so he worships no falsehood and they worship no truth, or it may simply parallel the two clauses.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا أنتم ﴾ فيما تستقبلون ﴿ عابدون ما أعبد ﴾ وذكر بلفظ ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first clause mā is not correctly read as a relative pronoun, whereas in the second it can mean that which.
rows.anchor: ولم يصح فى الأول من وصح فى الثانى ما بمعنى الذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their religion is polytheism and the Prophet's is monotheism; Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read the final yāʾ with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: لكم شرككم ولى توحيدى وبفتح الياء نافع وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet instructed Ibn Masʿūd to recite al-Kāfirūn in one rakʿa and al-Ikhlāṣ in the next; after the prayer he told him to ask and be answered.
rows.anchor: وروى أن ابن مسعود رضى الله عنه دخل المسجد والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is governed by sabbiḥ and refers to the future; foretelling the event before it happened is a sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: منصوب بسبح وهو لما يستقيل والإعلام بذلك قبل كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported to have been revealed at Minā during the days of tashrīq on the Farewell Pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وروى أنها نزلت في أيام التشريق بمنى في حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory means aid and triumph over an enemy, while conquest means opening lands; this may mean victory over the Arabs or Quraysh and the conquest of Mecca, or God's general victories and the opening of polytheist lands.
rows.anchor: النصر الاغاثة والاظهار على العدو والفتح فتح البلاد والمعنى نصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-raʾayta may be circumstantial from al-nās if it means saw or recognized, or a second object if it means knew; afwājan is circumstantial from the subject of yadkhulūn, and the answer to idhā is fa-sabbiḥ.
rows.anchor: هو حال من الناس على أن رأيت بمعنى أبصرت أو عرفت أو مفعول ثان على أنه بمعنى علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who entered in crowds are the Yemenites, who had previously entered Islam one or two at a time.
rows.anchor: ورأيت أهل اليمن يدخلون في ملة الإسلام جماعات كثيرة بعد ما كانوا يدخلون فيه واحدا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-sabbiḥ may mean say Subḥān Allāh while praising Him, or perform prayer; seek forgiveness humbly and self-effacingly, or persist in asking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فقل سبحان الله حامدا له أو فصل له ﴿ واستغفره ﴾ تواضعا وهضما للنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always been Tawwāb, abundantly accepting repentance; for servants, tawwāb describes frequent repentance.
rows.anchor: التواب الكثير القبول التوبة وفي صفة العباد الكثير الفعل للتوبة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When ʿUmar heard the sūra, he wept and said that completion signals departure; the Prophet lived two years afterward.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عمر رضى الله عنه لما سمعها بكى وقال الكمال دليل الزوال وعاش رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدها سنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat means destruction; the hands perished because, according to a report, Abū Lahab took a stone to throw at the Prophet, or the wording means his whole person perished as in the idiom about what one's hands earned.
rows.anchor: التباب الهلاك ومنه قولهم أشابه أم تابة أى هالكة من الهرم والمعنى هلكت يداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second tabba means he was destroyed and that this had happened; Ibn Masʿūd's reading wa-qad tab supports the completed event.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وتب وكان ذلك وحصل كقوله جزاني جزاه الله شر جزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the command to warn near relatives, the Prophet called people at Ṣafā and warned Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Banū Fihr that he was a warner before the Hour; Abū Lahab cursed him, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: روى أنه لما نزل وانذر عشيرتك الا قربين رقى الصفا وقال يا صباحاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab's kunya may be an honorific by which he was widely known, dislike of his name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, or a fitting reference to his future fiery fate.
rows.anchor: وإنما كناه والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بها دون الامم أو لكراهة اسمه فاسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a negator; mā kasab may be a relative noun or a verbal noun, referring to inherited and acquired wealth, old and new assets, or earnings.
rows.anchor: مرفوع وما موصولة أو مصدرية أي ومكسوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets what he acquired as his children.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ماكسب ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab reportedly said that if his nephew's message were true, he would ransom himself with his wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه كان يقول أن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقا فأنا أفتدى منه نفسي بمالي وولدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means he will enter the fire; al-Barjamī reports Abū Bakr's passive reading sayuṣlā, and the future particle warns that it will occur even if delayed.
rows.anchor: سيدخل سيصلى البرجمي عن أبي بكر والسين للوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is ablaze and burning.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذات لهب ﴾ توقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife is Umm Jamīl, daughter of Ḥarb and sister of Abū Sufyān; she carried thorns and brushwood to scatter at night on the Prophet's path.
rows.anchor: هي أم جميل بنت حرب أخت أبي سفيان ﴿ حمالة الحطب ﴾ كانت تحمل حزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says she carried gossip, kindling hostility among people.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانت تمشي بالنميمة فتشعل نار العداوة بين الناس

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads ḥammālata in the accusative as an insult, a reading the author prefers; with it, pausing at imraʾatihi is sound if the phrase is her predicate.
rows.anchor: ونصب عاصم حمالة الحطب على الشتم وأنا أحب هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī jīdihā may be a circumstantial phrase or another predicate; masad is a tightly twisted rope of palm fiber, leather, or other material.
rows.anchor: حال أو خبر آخر والمسد الذي قتل من الحبال فتلا شديدا من ليف كان أو جلدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She carries the thorn bundle tied around her neck like a wood gatherer, a humiliating depiction meant to distress her and her husband despite their former honor and wealth.
rows.anchor: وإنها تحمل تلك الحزمة من الشوك وتربطها في جيدها كما يفعل الحطابون تحقيرا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huwa is the pronoun of the affair: the proposition God is One is the affair itself; huwa is an initial subject whose predicate is the whole clause, which needs no resumptive pronoun.
rows.anchor: هو ضمير الشأن والله أحد هو الشأن كقولك هو زيد منطلق كانه قيل الشأن هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Quraysh asked Muhammad to describe the Lord to whom he called them, and this sūra was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما قالت قريش يا محمد صف لنا ربك الذي تدعونا اليه فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, huwa means the Lord you asked me to describe is God; aḥad is the predicate of an omitted subject and means one, from waḥd with its initial wāw changed to hamza.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا أحد خبر مبتدا محذوف أى هو أحد وهو بمعنى واحد وأصله وحد فقلبت الواو همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason rules out two gods: if one suffices to govern and create, the other is needless and deficient; if one cannot suffice, that one is deficient, and a needless, deficient being cannot be divine.
rows.anchor: كان كافيا كان الآخر ضائعا غيرمحتاج اليه وذلك نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one god could hide an act from another, the latter would be ignorant; if not, he would be unable to conceal it and thus powerless.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أما ان يقدر على ان يستر شيئا من أفعاله عن الآخر ولا يقدر فإن قدر لزم كون المستور عنه جاهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If neither god can create a possible thing both are incapable; if only one can, the other is not divine; if they cooperate they need one another.
rows.anchor: فان لم يقدر واحد منهما على إيجاده كان كل واحد منهما عاجزا والعاجز لا يكون الها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If either can create independently, both creating the same thing is impossible; if one creates it, the other either remains able to do the impossible or loses power and is dominated, so is not divine.
rows.anchor: فإذا أوجده أحدهما فأما أن يبقي الثاني قادرا عليه وهو محال لان ايجاد الموجود محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single creator's power is fulfilled rather than removed when it creates its object; one god disabling another would instead show subjection and incapacity.
rows.anchor: قلنا الواحد اذا اوجد مقدور نفسه فقد نفذت قدرته ومن نفذت قدرته لا يكون عاجزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣamad is an active form with passive meaning from the verb meaning to turn toward; it is the master to whom needs are directed, the self-sufficient God whom every creature needs.
rows.anchor: هو فعل بعنى مفعول من صمد اليه اذاقصده وهو السيد المصمود اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one they know as creator of the heavens, earth, and themselves, alone without partner; every creature turns to Him and none can dispense with Him, while He needs none.
rows.anchor: هو الله الذي تعرفونه وتقرون بأنه خالق السموات والأرض وخالقكم وهو واحد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not beget because He has no same-kind consort with whom He could reproduce; this is expressed elsewhere by asking how He could have a child without a consort.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يجانس حتى تكون له من جنسه صاحبة فيتوالدا وقد دل على هذا المعنى بقوله أنى يكون له ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God was not begotten because every begotten being is originated and corporeal; God is eternal with no beginning, since an originated being would need a maker and imply an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: لأن كل مولود محدث وجسم وهو قديم لا أول لوجوده أذ لو لم يكن قديما لكان حادثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not a body, which would be composite; if each part had perfect attributes each part would be a god, while lacking them would make parts subject to the signs of origination.
rows.anchor: وليس بجسم لأنه اسم للمتركب ولا يخلو حينئذ من ان يتصف كل جزء منه بصفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufuwan means an equal or counterpart; the sūra's sequence describes the Creator and His attributes, unity, self-sufficiency, eternity, and incomparable nature.
rows.anchor: ولم يكافئه أحد أى لم يماثله سالوه أن يصفه لهم فأوحى اليه ما يحتوى على صفاته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Him God and Creator entails power, knowledge, life, and all perfections, since their opposites are defects and signs of origination.
rows.anchor: خالق الأشياء وفاطرها وفى طى ذلك وصفه بأنه قادر عالم لأن الخالق يستدعى القدرة والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥad denies partners and identifies Him as sole creator and knower; al-ṣamad means all need Him and He needs none; not begetting denies likeness, not begotten denies origination, and no equal denies any counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقوله أحد وصف بالوحدانية ونفى الشريك وبأنه المتفرد بايجاد المعدومات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that denying an equal in the past does not deny one now is fallacious, since something originated cannot be equal to the eternal; the disbelievers' position reduces to association, likeness, and negation.
rows.anchor: ومن زعم أن نفى الكفء وهو المثل فى الماضى لا يدل على نفيه للحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh approves placing the circumstantial adverb first, though such complements usually follow, because the passage centers on denying any equal to God.
rows.anchor: واستحسن سيبويه تقديم الظرف إذا كان لغوا أى فضلة لأن التأخير مستحق للفضلات

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr prefers stopping at aḥad; ʿAbd al-Wārith says this was the reciters' inherited practice, while joining allows the tanwīn to be kasra-connected or dropped.
rows.anchor: على هذا أدركنا القراء واذا وصل نون وكسر أو حذف التنوين

rows.speaker: حمزة وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza and Khalaf read kafʾan with a still fāʾ and hamza; Ḥafṣ reads kafwan without hamza and with doubled form, while the other readers retain the hamza.
rows.anchor: كفؤا بسكون الفاء والهمزة حمزة وخلف كفوا مثقلة غير مهموزة حفص الباقون مثقلة مهموزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says reciting al-Ikhlāṣ equals a third of the Qurʾān because it covers the Qurʾān's topic of divine unity and attributes; this shows the distinction of theology, whose subject is most exalted.
rows.anchor: فى الحديث من قرأ سورة الاخلاص فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن لأن القرآن يشتمل على توحيد الله وذكر صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says that after hearing a man recite the sūra, the Prophet declared that Paradise was assured for him.
rows.anchor: وسمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يقرأ قل هو الله أحد فقال وجبت فقيل يا رسول الله ما وجبت

none: Bare sūra heading and section transition; no verse commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-falaq is explained as dawn, creation, or a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: أى الصبح أو الخلق أو هو وادفى جهنم أوجب فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created evil may refer to Hell and Satan; mā may be a relative pronoun with an omitted resumptive, or a verbal noun with khalq meaning creatures.
rows.anchor: أى النار والشيطان وما موصولة والعائد محذوف أو مصدرية ويكون الخلق بمعنى المخلوق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa reads min shar with tanwīn; on this reading mā and the verb form a genitive verbal noun explaining evil as the evil of creation, or mā may be extra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة رضى الله عنه من شر بالتنوين وما على هذا مع الفعل بتأويل المضدر فى موضع الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāsiq is night when darkness thickens, and wuqūb is darkness entering everything.
rows.anchor: الغاسق الليل إذا اعتكر ظلامه ووقوبه دخول ظلامه فى كل شئ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet took her hand, pointed to the moon, and told her to seek God's protection from its evil, identifying it as the darkening body when it sets or is eclipsed.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضى الله عنها أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدى فأشار إلى القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blowers may be women, souls, or groups of sorcerers who tie knots in threads, blow over them, and recite incantations; naft is blowing with saliva.
rows.anchor: النفاثات النساء أو النفوس أو الجماعات السواحر اللاتى يعقدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is evidence against the Muʿtazilites' denial that magic is real and has effects.
rows.anchor: والنفث النفخ مع ريق وهو دليل على بطلان قول المعتزلة فى انكار تحقيق السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envier harms another when envy appears and is acted upon; if kept hidden, it harms the envier through grief over another's joy.
rows.anchor: أى إذا ظهر حسده وعمل بمقتضاه لأنه إذا لم يظهر فلا ضرر يعود منه على من حسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special evils named after the general created evil are especially severe; envy is the worst and was the first sin in heaven by Iblīs and on earth by Qābīl.
rows.anchor: والاستعاذة من شر هذه الأشياء بعد الاستعاذة من شر ما خلق إشعار بأن شر هؤلاء أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine definite plural marks every blower as evil, whereas ghāsiq and ḥāsid are indefinite because not every dark night or envier is harmful; envy of good things may be praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وإنما عرف بعض المستعاذ منه ونكر بعضه لأن كل نفائة شريرة فلذا عرفت النفاثات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb al-nās means their nurturer and rectifier.
rows.anchor: أى مربيهم ومصلحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik al-nās means their owner and administrator of their affairs.
rows.anchor: مالكهم ومدبر أمورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāh al-nās means the one they worship; it explains Rabb al-nās, and repeating al-nās is apt because rabb and malik can describe others, whereas ilāh is uniquely God's.
rows.anchor: معبودهم ولم يكتف باظهار المضاف اليه مرة واحدة لأن قوله ملك الناس إله الناس عطف بيان لرب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is specially associated with people to honor them; the refuge is from the whisperer in their breasts, and He owns their affairs and is their God.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضيف الرب إلى الناس خاصة وإن كان رب كل مخلوق تشريفا لهم ولأن الاستعاذه وقعت من شر الموسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interprets the successive people as children, young adults, elders, the righteous, and the corrupt; the descriptions point respectively to nurturing, rule, worship, and Satan's desire to mislead the last groups.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد بالاول الاطفال ومعنى الربوبية يدل عليه وبالثانى الشبان ولفظ الملك المنبئ عن السياسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswās is a noun like zalzāl for an inaudible whisper; it denotes Satan, as if he were whispering itself, or one possessing whispers.
rows.anchor: هو اسم بمعنى الوسوسة كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة وأما المصدر فوسواس بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannās means one who habitually withdraws; Satan retreats when a person remembers God and returns to whisper when the person is heedless.
rows.anchor: الذى عادته أن يخنس منسوب إلى الخنوس وهو التأخر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that when a person remembers God, Satan withdraws, but when the person is heedless, he returns and whispers.
rows.anchor: لما روى عن سعيد بن جبير إذا ذكر الإنسان ربه خنس الشيطان وولى وإذا غفل رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may be genitive as an adjective; if parsed accusatively or nominatively as an insult, pausing at al-khannās is appropriate.
rows.anchor: فى محل الجر على الصفة أو الرفع أو النصب على الشتم وعلى هذين الوجهين يحسن الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explains the whisperer: devils are jinn and human, as another verse calls them human and jinn devils.
rows.anchor: بيان للذى يوسوس على أن الشيطان ضربان جنى وانسى كما قال شياطين الانس والجن

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr stood before a man and asked whether he had sought refuge from a human devil.
rows.anchor: وعن أبى ذر رضى الله عنه أنه قام لرجل هل تعوذت بالله من شيطان الانس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet was bewitched and became ill; two angels discussed the spell and named the Jewish Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam as the one who cast it.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام سحر فمرض فجاءه ملكان وهو نائم فقال أحدهما لصاحبه ما باله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spell used the Prophet's comb and hair in a palm spathe beneath a stone in the well of Dhū Arwān; Zubayr, ʿAlī, and ʿAmmār drained the water and retrieved it, finding eleven needle-pierced knots.
rows.anchor: قال بمشط ومشاطة فى جف طلعة تحت راعوفة فى بئر ذى أروان فانتبه صلى الله عليه وسلم فبعث زبيرا وعليا وعمارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Gabriel recited the two protective sūras, each verse untied a knot; at the last the Prophet felt as if released from a tether, while Gabriel prayed for his healing.
rows.anchor: فنزلت هاتان السورتان فكلما قرأ جبريل آية انحلت عقدة حتى قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking healing incantations is permissible when they use God's Book or the Prophet's words, not Syriac, Hebrew, or Indian formulas whose belief and reliance are impermissible.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جوز الاسترقاء بما كان من كتاب الله وكلام رسول عليه السلام لا بما كان بالسريانية والعبرانية والهندية

none: Verse text only; no commentary to record.
